findings.highlight: when her wound hasn’t even healed yet
findings.evidenceJa: 傷も癒えていないというのに
findings.governingReading: Taiga scolds Shirou for going out while his own wounds are still unhealed.
findings.explanation: The English assigns the wound to an unnamed woman, severing the bad-ending advice from Shirou’s injured condition.

findings.governingReading: Taiga objects that Illya’s gym bloomers are too blatant an appeal for attention.
findings.explanation: The untranslated loanword leaves the costume and the point of the meta joke opaque in English.

findings.governingReading: Taiga worries that Illya is stealing one of her scarce chances to be featured.
findings.explanation: The English treats spotlights as possessions and produces an unnatural version of a role-and-screen-time complaint.

findings.highlight: there’s isn’t even a need to compete
findings.governingReading: Taiga cheerfully concludes there was no need for them to compete.
findings.explanation: Two finite copulas remain in the same clause.

findings.governingReading: Taiga repeats a breezy expression of relief before declaring eternal best-friendship.
findings.explanation: The English adds a religious invocation and loses the deliberately repetitive rhythm.

findings.governingReading: After insisting she is not jealous, Taiga admits in oddly miniature terms that she is at least minimally curious.
findings.explanation: The English gives the basic degree but drops the conspicuous “minimum” phrasing that exposes her reversal.

findings.governingReading: Illya lists “kamakura” among a deliberately strange set of planned costumes without explaining it.
findings.explanation: The English invents a defined “style,” falsely resolving an intentionally opaque costume item.

findings.governingReading: Illya complains about adults voiding a specification sheet after it had been finalized.
findings.explanation: The concrete production-document joke becomes a generic reversed decision.

findings.governingReading: Taiga theatrically blames upper management for cutting her scenario.
findings.explanation: “Commanders” shifts the production-office joke toward a military hierarchy.

findings.evidenceJa: 狼藉者、そこになおれぃ
findings.governingReading: Taiga calls Rin an insolent ruffian and theatrically orders her to sit or kneel there and face punishment.
findings.explanation: The English replaces both mock-period terms with a static instruction and a generic insult.
